evidence: See docs/audit/keyboard-pass.md and keyboard-results.json for the recorded Tab sequence and reverse-navigation check.
user_impact: A keyboard user needs to reach the same main navigation actions without using a pointer.
remediation: Keep focus order aligned with the page structure; make each action a native link or button and provide a skip link.

evidence: Compare the focused elements in docs/screenshots/02-keyboard-focus.png and 03-navigation.png with the computed styles in keyboard-results.json.
user_impact: Without a clear focus cue, a sighted keyboard user can lose track of the current control.
remediation: Use a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible style and keep focus targets clear of sticky content.

wcag_reference: 2.4.6 Headings and Labels; 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
evidence: Review the heading list, heading skips and unnamed links recorded for the Services page in keyboard-results.json.
user_impact: A large department catalogue is harder to scan when headings or link names do not explain the grouping.
remediation: Use a logical heading sequence and descriptive link names; group related services semantically.

evidence: The FAQ describes text-size and contrast controls. The bounded Tab search is recorded in docs/audit/keyboard-pass.md.
user_impact: A visitor relying on text-size or contrast options needs to find and operate those controls from the keyboard.
remediation: Give each control a clear accessible name, a visible focus cue and a keyboard-operable state change.

evidence: The client uses a same-origin /api request; the Express server owns the service data and endpoint. See docs/architecture/README.md.
user_impact: Keeping the interface separate from storage makes later accessibility improvements and data changes easier to test.
remediation: Keep data access in the server and avoid database imports in React components.
